findings.title: Mixed custom and HTTP(S) schemes on Activity
findings.description: dif.tech.plata.platform.feature.root.RootActivity registers both a custom URI scheme (plata) and http/https. An attacker can trigger the http/https handler by crafting a universal link while also exploiting the custom-scheme handler that lacks verification.
findings.remediation: Separate http/https App Links from custom scheme handlers into distinct components. Ensure each uses appropriate verification (autoVerify for App Links, permission for custom).

findings.title: Deep link with wildcard/missing host: plata://*/*
findings.description: dif.tech.plata.platform.feature.root.RootActivity registers a deep link with no host restriction. Any host matches, meaning a malicious app or website can craft a URI with a malicious host to trigger this component, enabling open redirect and parameter injection.
findings.remediation: Always specify android:host with a specific domain. Avoid wildcard hosts. Use android:pathPattern to further restrict matching URIs.

findings.title: Deep link has no path restriction: https://plata.onelink.me/*
findings.description: dif.tech.plata.platform.feature.root.RootActivity matches any path under https://plata.onelink.me/. Without a pathPattern or pathPrefix, the entire URI space under this host is routed into the app, expanding the attack surface for parameter injection and open redirect.
findings.remediation: Add android:pathPrefix or android:pathPattern to restrict which paths trigger this component.

findings.title: Deep link has no path restriction: fbconnect://cct.dif.tech.plata/*
findings.description: com.facebook.CustomTabActivity matches any path under fbconnect://cct.dif.tech.plata/. Without a pathPattern or pathPrefix, the entire URI space under this host is routed into the app, expanding the attack surface for parameter injection and open redirect.
findings.remediation: Add android:pathPrefix or android:pathPattern to restrict which paths trigger this component.

findings.title: Hardcoded High-entropy hex string (possible key/IV/seed) detected
findings.description: A High-entropy hex string (possible key/IV/seed) was found hardcoded in the APK. Entropy: 3.74 bits/char. Hardcoded secrets can be trivially extracted by decompiling the APK.
findings.remediation: If this is key material, move it to Android Keystore or a remote KMS.

findings.title: Dangerous permission requires Data Safety disclosure: READ_CONTACTS
findings.description: Permission android.permission.READ_CONTACTS grants access to Contacts. Under GDPR Article 5, Google Play Data Safety policy, and CCPA, any collection of this data type must be disclosed in your privacy policy and Data Safety section.
findings.remediation: Ensure Contacts collection is disclosed in your Privacy Policy and Google Play Data Safety section. Only collect what is necessary.

findings.title: Location + network state combination enables device fingerprinting
findings.description: Combining ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION with ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE allows building a highly unique device fingerprint (location + WiFi SSIDs + network topology). This goes beyond normal location access.
findings.remediation: Justify why both permissions are required simultaneously. Avoid persisting or transmitting combined signals.
